title: Slow Horses
author: Mick Herron
note: Very funny, British and dry. Outrageous stories ofc
blurb: The Service's screw-ups are exiled to Slough House under the flatulent, brilliant Jackson Lamb; a staged kidnapping drags them back into play.

title: Dead Lions
author: Mick Herron
note: Nostalgic of le Carré
blurb: An old Cold War spook turns up dead on a bus, and Lamb suspects a Soviet sleeper network was never switched off.

title: Real Tigers
author: Mick Herron
note: Fun, easy read. Characters are special
blurb: One of the slow horses is kidnapped as leverage in a power struggle inside the Service itself.

title: London Rules
author: Mick Herron
note: More political intrigue, still funny
blurb: A terror campaign follows a stolen playbook, while Westminster politics eat themselves.

title: Joe Country
author: Mick Herron
note: Not as good as the others
blurb: The slow horses go to Wales after a dead agent's son goes missing; the body count is unusually high.

title: Slough House
author: Mick Herron
note: Exciting. Good diversion
blurb: Post-Brexit paranoia; the slow horses are being quietly erased from the record and picked off.

title: Bad Actors
author: Mick Herron
note: Doesn't feel too far fetched
blurb: A government think-tank adviser vanishes, and a Russian operation surfaces inside No. 10.

title: Clown Town
author: Mick Herron
note: Always entertaining books
blurb: The most recent Slough House novel — Lamb's crew against a buried Service scandal.

title: The Catch
author: Mick Herron
note: Very different mood from others in the series.
blurb: Short entry in the Slough House universe following John Bachelor, the milkman who minds retired agents.

title: The Secret Hours
author: Mick Herron
note: Nostalgai for old spy novels
blurb: An inquiry into historical Service misconduct unearths a disastrous Berlin operation.

title: Nobody Walks
author: Mick Herron
note: Hard to read
blurb: Tom Bettany comes back to London to find out who killed his estranged son.

title: Absolute Friends
author: John le Carré
note: Useful idiots, unfortunately
blurb: Two friends from the 1960s radical left are used and discarded by intelligence services, ending in the post-9/11 era.

title: The Honourable Schoolboy
author: John le Carré
note: Entertaining
blurb: Smiley, rebuilding the ruined Circus, follows a Soviet money trail into Hong Kong and Southeast Asia.

title: The Karla Trilogy Digital Collection Featuring George Smiley
author: John le Carré
note: Only the paranoid survive
blurb: Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy, The Honourable Schoolboy and Smiley's People collected — Smiley's long duel with Karla.

title: A Legacy of Spies
author: John le Carré
note: Sadder than the rest
blurb: Peter Guillam, retired to Brittany, is hauled back to answer for the operation behind The Spy Who Came in from the Cold.

title: All the Old Knives
author: Olen Steinhauer
note: Don't know if I'd recommend. Felt like without a point.
blurb: Two ex-lovers from the CIA's Vienna station have dinner years later and relitigate a hijacking that went wrong — and who leaked.

title: The Last Tourist
author: Olen Steinhauer
note: Totally ok to read
blurb: Weaver and the UN's Tourists resurface against a private intelligence network.

title: A Spy Among Friends
author: Ben Macintyre
note: Non fiction written as fiction. What a boys club the UK was/is!!
blurb: Kim Philby's betrayal told through his friendship with fellow MI6 officer Nicholas Elliott.

title: The Kill Artist
author: Daniel Silva
note: Meh
blurb: An Israeli art restorer and former assassin is pulled out of retirement to hunt a Palestinian operative.

title: The Peacock and the Sparrow
author: I.S. Berry
note: Kind of meh. Disappointing plot in the end
blurb: A burned-out CIA officer in Bahrain during the Arab Spring falls for a local artist; written by a former CIA analyst.

title: Red, White, Blue
author: Lea Carpenter
note: Woulnd't necessarily recommend. POintless
blurb: A woman investigating her CIA father's death intercuts with the officer who knew him; more literary than procedural.

title: The Way of the Knife
author: Mark Mazzetti
blurb: How the CIA turned from spying to killing after 9/11 — drones, JSOC, and the blurred line between them.

title: The Collaborators
author: Michael Idov
note: Exciting!
blurb: A CIA officer and a Russian woman are drawn together across a defection plot.

title: Playing to the Edge
author: Michael V. Hayden
note: Good look at "the other side" of the argument against US surveillance and abuse of power. 'Truly think they think they did the right thing most of the time. Democracy leaves more flexibility to the amoral, on both sides of the law.
blurb: Michael Hayden's memoir of running the NSA and CIA through the surveillance and interrogation years.

title: The Kremlin Letter
author: Noel Behn
note: It's funny when you read this, you immediately feel it's from a different time.
blurb: A Cold War team is assembled to retrieve an unauthorised letter from Moscow; bleak and much-praised 1966 novel.

title: The Good Assassin
author: Paul Vidich
blurb: A former CIA man goes to 1950s Cuba to check on an old colleague as Batista's regime rots.

title: The Lions of Lucerne
author: Brad Thor
note: Like a bond movie book. Very cliche
blurb: Secret Service agent Harvath hunts the team that ambushed the President's ski detail in Utah.

title: The Last Patriot
author: Brad Thor
note: These can fill time
blurb: Harvath chases a lost passage of the Koran that jihadists will kill to suppress.

title: Use of Force
author: Brad Thor
blurb: A drowned migrant boat leads Harvath to an ISIS cell planning a European attack.

title: Black Ice
author: Brad Thor
blurb: Harvath spots a man who should be dead in Oslo; Russian ambitions in the Arctic follow.

title: Dead Fall
author: Brad Thor
blurb: Harvath pursues a marauding Russian unit through Ukraine.

title: Fever Beach
author: Carl Hiaasen
note: Kind of funny
blurb: Florida satire: a dim white supremacist, dark money and a couple of decent people trying to stop it.

title: Bad Monkey
author: Carl Hiaasen
note: Funny, read it but didn't see the series
blurb: A demoted Florida detective, a severed arm in a freezer, insurance fraud and a very bad monkey.

title: The Accident
author: Chris Pavone
blurb: An anonymous manuscript that would destroy a media mogul moves through publishing, killing people as it goes.

title: The Expats
author: Chris Pavone
note: Somewhat ok
blurb: An ex-CIA officer playing housewife in Luxembourg realises the couple befriending them is running a game.

author: Elliot Ackerman, Admiral James Stavridis, USN
note: Really not far from plausible. I can point to companies building the technologies in use for most of the twists, or protecting against the attacks mentioned.
blurb: A US–China naval confrontation escalates to nuclear exchange, told from many command chairs.

author: Elliot Ackerman, Admiral James Stavridis, USN
note: Love the space piratery
blurb: Sequel: an American president dies suddenly and an AI singularity looms.

title: Open Carry
author: Marc Cameron
note: Made me want to see Alaska
blurb: A deputy US marshal works a disappearance in the Alaskan wilderness.

title: Red Winter
author: Marc Cameron
note: Meh
blurb: Cold War-era Jack Ryan: a Soviet defector offer forces a Moscow operation.

title: The Mysterious Affair at Styles
author: Agatha Christie
note: I've read Christie since I was a child and enjoyed each of them greatly
blurb: Poirot's debut: a poisoning at an English country house during WWI.

title: Cold Blood
author: Alex Shaw
note: Meh
blurb: Ex-SAS Snow against Russian operations in Ukraine.

title: Open Season
author: C. J. Box
note: Captivating
blurb: A Wyoming game warden finds bodies near his woodpile and an endangered species cover-up.

title: Traitor
author: Chris Ryan
blurb: Chris Ryan military thriller — SAS-flavoured operation against an insider betrayal.

title: Whalefall
author: Daniel Kraus
note: Very poetic and biologically accurate description of what it would be like to be swallowed by a whale, but is about loss and childhood
blurb: A teenage diver looking for his father's remains is swallowed by a sperm whale, with an hour of air.

title: Northern Spy
author: Flynn Berry
note: Beautiful about conviction and what you think is right or wrong
blurb: A BBC producer in Belfast discovers her sister is in the IRA.

title: The Fist of God
author: Frederick Forsyth
note: interesting political parallels to today
blurb: Gulf War: SAS and intelligence hunt Saddam's supergun and a rumoured superweapon.

title: Fool Me Once
author: Harlan Coben
note: meh
blurb: A widowed ex-soldier sees her murdered husband alive on the nanny cam.

title: Homecoming
author: Kate Morton
blurb: A journalist returns to Australia and reopens a 1959 family killing that has shaped three generations.

title: Three Assassins
author: Kotaro Isaka
note: I need to read more japanese books
blurb: Tokyo contract killers circle a grieving man out for revenge; dark comedy.

title: The Last Thing He Told Me
author: Laura Dave
blurb: A man vanishes leaving a note reading 'protect her'; his wife and teenage stepdaughter unpick his past.

title: Ghost Fleet
author: P. W. Singer, August Cole
note: Not even crazy to believe
blurb: Near-future US–China war fought with hacked F-35s and mothballed ships; every gadget footnoted to real tech.

title: The Trees
author: Percival Everett
note: Interesting vibe for sure.
blurb: Bodies keep appearing beside white murder victims in Mississippi, each resembling Emmett Till; savage satire.

title: Shadow War
author: Sean McFate
note: A lot of Ukraine relevance
blurb: A mercenary runs a deniable operation in Ukraine.

title: Silver Nitrate
author: Silvia Moreno-Garcia
note: Mexican goth ghost stories with Nazies
blurb: Mexico City sound editor and a washed-up horror director find a Nazi occultist's cursed unfinished film.

title: The Old Man
author: Thomas Perry
note: I think this was a series?
blurb: A man who has hidden for thirty years after stealing government money is found, and turns out to be very hard to kill.

title: The Ferryman
author: Justin Cronin
note: Frightening. Not hard to squint at society and recognize patterns
blurb: On the island utopia of Prospera the retired are ferried away for renewal; a man starts noticing the seams.

title: The Passage
author: Justin Cronin
note: Oh, loved these series. Less so for the vampires and more for the characters and dynamics
blurb: A military virus trial creates immortal vampiric 'virals'; the story jumps a century to the survivors.

title: The Twelve
author: Justin Cronin
note: Great series
blurb: The survivors hunt the twelve original virals to end the plague.

title: The City of Mirrors
author: Justin Cronin
note: Society starts over
blurb: Conclusion: Zero's own story, and the last stand of the colony.

title: Walking to Aldebaran
author: Adrian Tchaikovsky
note: Very scary and interesting
blurb: An astronaut lost inside an alien artefact narrates his wanderings with increasingly alarming cheerfulness.

title: Children of Time
author: Adrian Tchaikovsky
note: Spiders are not scary. Whenever I read about alien intelligence I think of LLMs
blurb: A terraforming experiment goes wrong and uplifts spiders instead of monkeys, while humanity's last ark ship approaches.

title: Children of Ruin
author: Adrian Tchaikovsky
note: Less novel than #1
blurb: Sequel: a second terraformed world, octopuses, and something far stranger in the water.

title: Project Hail Mary
author: Andy Weir
note: This is amazing. Loved it
blurb: A man wakes alone on a starship with amnesia, tasked with saving the Sun — and finds company.

title: The Martian
author: Andy Weir
note: Of course, classic by now
blurb: Mark Watney, stranded on Mars, science-problem-solves his way toward rescue.

title: Artemis
author: Andy Weir
note: Not as good as the others
blurb: A smuggler in the Moon's only city takes a sabotage job that goes badly wrong.

title: Ninefox Gambit
author: Yoon Ha Lee
note: Seems unnecessarily complicated and gruesome (torturers as a guild).
blurb: Calendrical warfare, heretic fortresses, and a disgraced captain sharing her skull with an undead traitor general.

title: Raven Stratagem
author: Yoon Ha Lee
note: Interesting personality-ego mixes
blurb: Jedao seizes a swarm and the hexarchate scrambles to work out what he actually wants.

title: Revenant Gun
author: Yoon Ha Lee
blurb: A teenage Jedao wakes in a stranger's body as the hexarchate fractures.

title: To Sleep in a Sea of Stars
author: Christopher Paolini
note: We can rise above ourselves
blurb: A xenobiologist touches an alien relic that bonds to her and starts an interstellar war.

title: Fractal Noise
author: Christopher Paolini
note: This was very interesting. You don't need much complexity for something to be hard and captivating. About loss
blurb: A perfectly circular hole is found on an alien world; four people walk toward it as the expedition disintegrates.

title: The Bayern Agenda
author: Dan Moren
note: Kind of fun read, less about strategy
blurb: A wisecracking operative goes undercover in a bank on a neutral world.

title: The Aleph Extraction
author: Dan Moren
note: Oceans eleven but space?
blurb: The team infiltrates a crew of thieves to steal an artefact.

title: Red Rising
author: Pierce Brown
note: Oppression is too obvious
blurb: A Red miner on Mars learns his caste's sacrifice is a lie and is surgically remade to infiltrate the Gold elite.

title: Golden Son
author: Pierce Brown
note: More interesting than #1, more strategy and space opera-esque
blurb: Darrow among the Golds, playing a much longer and bloodier game.

title: The Wrong Stars
author: Tim Pratt
note: Funny but also the Axiom aliens are truly interesting
blurb: A salvage crew finds a derelict sleeper ship and an alien with a very optimistic account of the galaxy.

title: The Dreaming Stars
author: Tim Pratt
note: Good follow up
blurb: The White Raven crew hides in the asteroid belt while working out how to fight the Axiom.

title: The Rift Uprising
author: Amy S. Foster
note: Meh
blurb: A teenage soldier guards a portal between parallel Earths and starts remembering what was done to her.

title: A Memory Called Empire
author: Arkady Martine
note: I had higher hopees for this one tbh
blurb: An ambassador from a small station arrives at a devouring empire's capital carrying her murdered predecessor's memories.

title: Dark Matter
author: Blake Crouch
note: So and so
blurb: A physicist is abducted by a version of himself who took the other path, and has to find his way home through the multiverse.

title: Empire of Silence
author: Christopher Ruocchio
note: I'd like to continue this series
blurb: Hadrian Marlowe narrates, from captivity, how he became the man who destroyed a sun and a species.

title: Flowers for Algernon
author: Daniel Keyes
note: One of the best books I read. Highly recommended. Should induce empathy with anyone
blurb: Charlie Gordon's progress reports track his surgically raised intelligence and its loss.

title: Change Agent
author: Daniel Suarez
note: Quite interesting
blurb: Black-market CRISPR in Southeast Asia; an agent wakes up wearing the body of the crime lord he was hunting.

title: City of Orange
author: David Yoon
note: Well worth a read!
blurb: A man wakes injured in a wasteland with no memory of who he is or what ended the world.

title: Station Eleven
author: Emily St. John Mandel
note: I like apocalypse. This is a beautifully written one
blurb: A flu kills most of humanity; twenty years on a Travelling Symphony performs Shakespeare across the Great Lakes.

title: Dune Messiah
author: Frank Herbert
note: Love Dune
blurb: Paul Atreides, twelve years into his jihad, is trapped by his own prescience and myth.

title: The Anomaly
author: Hervé Le Tellier
note: Very french, terrifying, and bleak
blurb: A Paris–New York flight lands twice, months apart, with two identical sets of passengers.

title: Second Foundation
author: Isaac Asimov
note: Ultimate intelligence doesn't need physical violence to dominate
blurb: The Mule hunts the hidden Second Foundation of mentalists.

title: The City of Ember
author: Jeanne DuPrau
note: Kind of cute, exciting story of repressed people
blurb: An underground city's lights are failing and two children find instructions for a way out.

title: Annihilation
author: Jeff VanderMeer
note: This is an interesting psycho-hallucinatory dystopian horror story.
blurb: The twelfth expedition into Area X — a biologist, a psychologist, a surveyor, and a tower going down.

title: Terminal Alliance
author: Jim C. Hines
note: Quite funny, and inventive
blurb: The janitorial crew is all that's left to fly the ship after everyone else is incapacitated; comedy.

title: Flux
author: Jinwoo Chong
note: Ultimately about loss and grief, seen through technology mechanisms and capitalist structures
blurb: A boy, a man and an ageing actor braid together around a collapsed tech startup and a time-slipping grief.

title: The Forever War
author: Joe Haldeman
note: Finally a sci-fi book that takes time dilation seriously!
blurb: Relativistic time dilation means every tour returns soldiers to an Earth centuries stranger than the one they left.

title: Saturn Run
author: John Sandford, Ctein
note: Loved the engineering!
blurb: An alien ship parks at Saturn and the US and China race to reach it first; hard-SF engineering throughout.

title: In Ascension
author: Martin MacInnes
note: We know little of the sea
blurb: A Dutch marine biologist moves from an ocean trench to a mission beyond the solar system; quiet and enormous.

title: Ascension
author: Nicholas Binge
blurb: An impossible mountain appears in the Pacific; the climb goes very strange, told in letters.

title: Titanium Noir
author: Nick Harkaway
note: This reminded me of the first Altered Carbon, except they're a different biohacking kind
blurb: Hardboiled detective in a world where the ultra-rich dose themselves into giants.

title: Woken Furies
author: Richard K. Morgan
blurb: Kovacs returns to his home world Harlan's World for revenge, in a body that isn't his.

title: The Men
author: Sandra Newman
blurb: Every person with a Y chromosome vanishes from Earth in an instant, and the world that remains reckons with it.

title: Ode to the Half-Broken
author: Suzanne Palmer
blurb: Recent Suzanne Palmer novel — I can't reliably summarise this one, please fill in.

title: Fool's Assassin
author: Robin Hobb
note: Classic fantasy. Has it all
blurb: Fitz, in quiet retirement at Withywoods, has that peace destroyed.

title: Fool's Quest
author: Robin Hobb
note: Recommend
blurb: Fitz searches for his abducted daughter Bee while the Fool lies broken.

title: Assassin's Fate
author: Robin Hobb
note: As often with series, I enjoyed the first more
blurb: The conclusion — Clerres, dragons, and the end of Fitz's story.

title: Amongst Our Weapons
author: Ben Aaronovitch
blurb: Peter Grant investigates a killing tied to a set of magical rings and an avenging figure.

title: Stone and Sky
author: Ben Aaronovitch
note: Very vibey scottish scenery
blurb: Peter Grant takes the family to Scotland; magical trouble follows into Aberdeen waters.

title: The Graveyard Book
author: Neil Gaiman
note: Actually a detective/romance/coming of age story
blurb: A toddler whose family is murdered is raised by the ghosts of a graveyard.

title: Norse Mythology
author: Neil Gaiman
note: I didn't learn so much new from this, given that we learn this stuff in school in Sweden
blurb: Gaiman retells the Norse myths from Yggdrasil to Ragnarok in plain, funny prose.

title: The Color of Magic
author: Terry Pratchett
note: I was very late to Discworld. It's weird and funny, as you'd think
blurb: Rincewind the failed wizard escorts the Disc's first tourist; the flat world on four elephants introduced.

title: The Light Fantastic
author: Terry Pratchett
note: We all carry an indescribable spell in our heads which can destroy the world
blurb: Rincewind carries a spell that's the only thing that can save the Disc from a red star.

title: The Great When
author: Alan Moore
note: Terrifying and exciting
blurb: Post-war London bookshop boy finds a book that doesn't exist in this world, opening onto a second, older London.

title: The Black Prism
author: Brent Weeks
note: Quite liked this. The magic system makes zero sense, but interesting societal structure
blurb: Gavin Guile, the Prism who can split light into magic, has five years to live and a secret son.

title: Ordinary Monsters
author: J. M. Miro
note: A story of the weird and outcasts
blurb: Victorian children with strange powers are gathered to a Scottish institute, pursued by something worse.

title: Furies of Calderon
author: Jim Butcher
blurb: Roman-styled empire where everyone commands elemental furies — except young Tavi, whose valley is about to be invaded.

title: The Bright Sword
author: Lev Grossman
note: Lev makes humans so human, in magical conditions.
blurb: A young knight arrives at Camelot two weeks after Arthur dies, and the leftovers must hold Britain together.

title: A Broken Blade
author: Melissa Blair
note: Quite entertaining.
blurb: A half-elf assassin is sent to spy on the tyrant king.

title: A Master of Djinn
author: P. Djèlí Clark
note: Feels forced
blurb: 1912 Cairo where magic returned: an agent of the Ministry investigates a cult murder and an impostor al-Jahiz.

title: Babel
author: R.F. Kuang
note: Author writes about the importance of words and magical properties of language
blurb: Oxford's translation institute powers the empire with silver bars and lost meaning; a Cantonese orphan is trained into it.

title: Hollow City
author: Ransom Riggs
blurb: The peculiar children escape to 1940 London to find a way of restoring Miss Peregrine from bird form.

title: Foundryside
author: Robert Jackson Bennett
note: Interesting magic concept
blurb: Scriving lets objects be argued into behaving differently; a thief steals a key that talks back.

title: The City of Brass
author: S. A. Chakraborty
note: Diverting
blurb: An 18th-century Cairo con artist accidentally summons a djinn warrior and is dragged to a hidden magical city.

title: A Day of Fallen Night
author: Samantha Shannon
blurb: Prequel to The Priory of the Orange Tree: four women across the world as the wyrms wake.

title: A Court of Thorns and Roses
author: Sarah J. Maas
note: Couldn't finish this trash
blurb: A huntress is taken to the faerie lands in payment for a kill; Beauty and the Beast with courts and curses.

title: On Tennis
author: David Foster Wallace
note: One of the most beautiful, funny, books of human observation and analysis I read
blurb: Five essays on tennis, including Federer as religious experience and his own junior career in Midwest crosswinds.

title: The Pale King
author: David Foster Wallace
blurb: Unfinished posthumous novel set in an IRS processing centre in Peoria — boredom, attention and civic duty.

title: Intermezzo
author: Sally Rooney
note: Love, grief, ego. Unhidden political agenda
blurb: Two brothers — a chess player and a lawyer — grieve their father badly and differently.

title: Normal People
author: Sally Rooney
note: Love, ego, class and intellect
blurb: Marianne and Connell circle each other from a Sligo school to Trinity, always slightly mistimed.

title: Distant Light
author: Antonio Moresco
note: Very moving. Beautiful and sad. Reminded me of some of Murakami's scenery
blurb: A hermit in an abandoned village sees a single light across the valley each night and goes to find its source.

title: Lovely, Dark and Deep
author: Claudia Cain
note: Meh
blurb: Small-press novel I can't reliably summarise — please fill in.

title: Twist
author: Colum McCann
note: Subsea cables seem to be a thinly veiled metaphor here. Some degrowth romanticism ongoing...
blurb: A journalist joins a ship repairing undersea internet cables off West Africa; its chief goes missing.

title: The Book of I
author: David Greig
note: A lot of fun for a short novel
blurb: Recent David Greig novel — I can't reliably summarise this one, please fill in.

title: How to Build a Boat
author: Elaine Feeney
blurb: A neurodivergent Irish boy determined to build a perpetual motion machine, and the two teachers who orbit him.

title: For Whom the Bell Tolls
author: Ernest Hemingway
note: Again and again, I forget what good writing looks like, until I'm confronted with it again and immediately recognize it.
blurb: An American dynamiter with Republican guerrillas has three days to blow a bridge in the Spanish Civil War.

title: Reward System
author: Jem Calder
note: Some of the millenial, gen Z despair and hopelessness around love, wealth and catastrophy-anxiety
blurb: Linked stories about young people, work, apps and inertia in contemporary London.

title: Big Swiss
author: Jen Beagin
blurb: A transcriptionist for a sex therapist recognises a client's voice in a dog park and lies her way into her life.

title: Slaughterhouse-Five
author: Kurt Vonnegut
note: Amazing names and depictions of diseases which had no names at the time
blurb: Billy Pilgrim comes unstuck in time between Dresden's firebombing and the aliens of Tralfamadore.

title: Thrust
author: Lidia Yuknavitch
blurb: A time-travelling 'carrier' moves between eras around the making of the Statue of Liberty.

title: The Blind Assassin
author: Margaret Atwood
note: The past was grim; M.A. is a brilliant storyteller
blurb: Iris Chase's memoir wraps a pulp SF story wrapped inside a novel published under her dead sister's name.

title: Sérotonine
author: Michel Houellebecq
note: France is really like this, to a degree. And man definitely is.
blurb: A depressed agronomist on a libido-killing antidepressant drifts through a decaying rural France.

title: Munich
author: Robert Harris
note: Echos current events
blurb: Two former friends, one British and one German, at the 1938 Munich conference.

title: Red Famine
author: Anne Applebaum
blurb: Stalin's deliberate starvation of Ukraine in 1932–33 and the long cover-up.

title: Freedom's Forge
author: Arthur Herman
blurb: How American business converted to arms production and out-produced the Axis.

title: The Road
author: Christopher Hadley
blurb: Landscape history tracing a Roman road across the English countryside and everything layered on it.

title: Taming the Street
author: Diana B. Henriques
note: Wall street was REALLY wild pre-depression. Truly criminal enterprise
blurb: FDR's fight to regulate Wall Street and the birth of the SEC.

title: The Splendid and the Vile
author: Erik Larson
note: I was never a big biography-reader, but this was amazing. I get why Churchill attracts people. Memorable story: When we was appointed PM he apparently wrote in his diary that he was relieved to finally know that someone competent (i.e., himself) was in charge of the war effort!
blurb: Churchill's first year in office and the Blitz, told through diaries and family life.

title: Red Plenty
author: Francis Spufford
blurb: Half novel, half history: the brief Soviet moment when cybernetic planning looked like it might out-produce capitalism.

title: The Shortest History of Germany
author: James Hawes
note: Germany has been divided most of the time, and continues to be so.
blurb: Brisk polemical sweep arguing an east/west fault line runs through German history.

title: A History of Warfare
author: John Keegan
blurb: Argues war is an expression of culture rather than politics by other means, from stone age to nuclear.

title: The Gates of Europe
author: Serhii Plokhy
blurb: A thousand years of Ukrainian history from Kyivan Rus to the present.

title: Abundance
author: Ezra Klein, Derek Thompson
note: I don't know. A lot of the arguemnts make a lot of sense, and I agree with it, yet I was somehow disappointed by what it achieves
blurb: Argues the left should focus on building — housing, energy, infrastructure — rather than blocking.

title: Volga Blues
author: Marzio G. Mian
note: We need to understand Russia better. Consuming only propaganda (from either side) will not help us.
blurb: A journey down the Volga as a portrait of contemporary Russia.

title: Some People Need Killing
author: Patricia Evangelista
note: Criminal state head suppressess freedom
blurb: A Filipino reporter's account of Duterte's drug war and the people who did the killing.

title: The End of the World is Just the Beginning
author: Peter Zeihan
note: This certainly feels true but has holes in its arguments. Most of the structural observations can't be argued with, and I agree, but the there's no good argument for why it's happening now, or why we won't be able to adapt.
blurb: Demographics and the end of American naval security mean deglobalisation and a much poorer world.

title: When the Heavens Went on Sale
author: Ashlee Vance
note: Great intro
blurb: Rocket Lab, Astra, Firefly and Planet Labs — the scrappy, chaotic new space industry.

title: The Hard Thing About Hard Things
author: Ben Horowitz
note: Should have read earlier
blurb: Horowitz on the parts of running a company nobody writes about — layoffs, demotions, wartime CEOs.

title: How Big Things Get Done
author: Bent Flyvbjerg, Dan Gardner
note: This is amazing. Loved it, and I wish more statesmen would read it too
blurb: Why megaprojects blow up, and the fixes: think slow act fast, modularity, reference-class forecasting.

title: Range
author: David Epstein
note: Rings very true
blurb: Generalists and late specialisers outperform in complex 'wicked' domains.

title: Apple in China
author: Patrick McGee
note: Fascinating. Highly recommended. Ties are much tighter than I imagined, and dependencies are insane
blurb: How Apple trained China's electronics industry and made itself hostage to it.

title: Zero to One
author: Peter Thiel, Blake Masters
note: Should have read earlier, will re-read
blurb: Thiel's Stanford lectures: competition is for losers, build monopolies, go from zero to one.

title: The Art of Doing Science and Engineering
author: Richard W. Hamming
blurb: Hamming's Naval Postgraduate lectures on doing work that still matters in thirty years — includes 'You and Your Research'.

title: The Infinite Game
author: Simon Sinek
blurb: Sinek argues business is an infinite game and finite-minded leadership destroys companies.

title: The Spirit of Terrorism
author: Jean Baudrillard
blurb: Baudrillard on 9/11 as an event the system provoked against itself.

title: The Vital Illusion
author: Jean Baudrillard
blurb: Three lectures on cloning, virtual reality and the disappearance of death and the real.

title: After Virtue
author: Alasdair MacIntyre
blurb: Modern moral argument is unresolvable because we're using fragments of a lost Aristotelian tradition.

title: The Burnout Society
author: Byung-Chul Han
note: Modern society avoids negativity to such degree that we become depressed, hyperactive, drowning in endless possibility. We can do anything, yet never achieve closure. Never being able to finish, always struggling for more, through complete fungibility of identity. Exit disciplinary society and enter self-controlling, self-determining society further focuses ourselves on our narcissistic selves.
blurb: We moved from a disciplinary society to an achievement society, where we exploit ourselves willingly.

title: This Is Water
author: David Foster Wallace
note: The trenches of adult life
blurb: The Kenyon commencement address on default settings, attention, and choosing what to think about.

title: The Scout Mindset
author: Julia Galef
note: Helpful but not revelatory or especially novel
blurb: Seeing accurately rather than defending a position — scout versus soldier thinking.

title: How to Avoid a Climate Disaster
author: Bill Gates
note: Clear and pretty accurate, yet we haven't solved it
blurb: Gates on the 51 billion tons, green premiums, and which technologies actually matter.

title: Seven Brief Lessons on Physics
author: Carlo Rovelli
note: Made me love physics more. Should have read during Uni
blurb: Relativity, quanta, cosmology and time in seven very short essays.

title: The Grid
author: Gretchen Bakke
note: Meh, somewhat interesting history, but as with many of these popular books very info-sparse
blurb: The American electrical grid as an ageing, improvised machine that renewables are straining.

title: The Future of Humanity
author: Michio Kaku
note: Very pop-sciey and nothing new
blurb: Terraforming, starships and digital immortality as humanity's route off Earth.

title: Pandora's Lab
author: Paul A. Offit MD
blurb: Seven scientific breakthroughs — from opiates to eugenics — that did enormous harm.

title: What If?
author: Randall Munroe
note: long time fan
blurb: Absurd hypothetical questions answered with real physics and stick figures.

title: Elon Musk
author: Walter Isaacson
note: Explains a lot. Still impressive
blurb: Isaacson's access-driven biography through Twitter, SpaceX and Tesla.

title: Leonardo da Vinci
author: Walter Isaacson
note: Da Vinci came from a family of notaries, was a bastard, never went to school and could barely do basic algebra. Notoriously bad at keeping deadlines or finishing stuff. Dissected many humans and animals to understand them. "Investigate the woodpecker's tounge". Deeeeeeply curious about everything. Openly gay
blurb: Isaacson's biography built from the notebooks, linking Leonardo's art to his anatomy and engineering.

title: Vanderbilt
author: Anderson Cooper, Katherine Howe
blurb: Anderson Cooper on his mother's family — the rise and self-destruction of the Vanderbilt fortune.

title: A Sacred Oath
author: Mark T. Esper
blurb: Trump's Secretary of Defense on trying to hold the Pentagon steady in 2019–20.

title: Greenlights
author: Matthew McConaughey
note: Best listened to read by McConaughey. Some trad-leftish, intellectual cowboy stuff, but very inspiring.
blurb: McConaughey's diaries turned into a book about taking the green lights when they come.

title: The Salt Path
author: Raynor Winn
note: Beautiful. Listened to this during my long runs leading up to Boston
blurb: A couple, homeless and one of them terminally diagnosed, walk the 630-mile South West Coast Path.

title: Con/Artist
author: Tony Tetro, Giampiero Ambrosi
note: Amazing story about the business of art, the mastery of various crafts and morality.
blurb: A master forger's account of forty years faking Chagall, Dalí and Caravaggio.

title: How to Have a Good Day
author: Caroline Webb
blurb: Behavioural science applied to the working day — priorities, attention, conversations.

title: The Mindful Athlete
author: George Mumford
blurb: The mindfulness coach to Jordan's Bulls and Kobe's Lakers on flow and performance.

title: Dino-Valentine's Day
author: Lisa Wheeler
blurb: Children's picture book — dinosaurs celebrate Valentine's Day. Almost certainly a read-aloud, not yours.

title: The Book You Wish Your Parents Had Read
author: Philippa Perry
note: Gotcha
blurb: Psychotherapist on parenting as repair — your own childhood, ruptures, and how to mend them.

title: How to Fail at Almost Everything and Still Win Big
author: Scott Adams
blurb: Adams on systems over goals, talent stacks, and failing usefully.

title: The Agony of Eros
author: Byung-Chul Han
blurb: Han argues that a culture of relentless self-optimisation has erased the Other, and with it the possibility of eros, leaving only narcissism and depression.

title: The Structure of Scientific Revolutions
author: Thomas S. Kuhn
blurb: The book that gave us the paradigm shift: science advances not by steady accumulation but by crises in which an old framework collapses and a new one replaces it.

title: Technological Revolutions and Financial Capital
author: Carlota Perez
blurb: Each technological revolution runs the same arc — installation, a financial bubble, a crash, then deployment — a roughly fifty-year rhythm from canals to microchips.

title: The Man Who Solved the Market
author: Gregory Zuckerman

title: The Spy Who Came In from the Cold
author: John le Carré

title: The Slow Regard of Silent Things
author: Patrick Rothfuss

title: My Year of Rest and Relaxation
author: Ottessa Moshfegh

title: The City in the Middle of the Night
author: Charlie Jane Anders

title: The Merchant and the Alchemist's Gate
author: Ted Chiang

title: Once Upon a Time in the North
author: Philip Pullman

title: War! What Is It Good For?
author: Ian Morris

title: The Terrors of Ice and Darkness
author: Christoph Ransmayr

title: A Political History of the World
author: Jonathan Holslag

title: If on a Winter's Night a Traveler
author: Italo Calvino

title: All the Birds in the Sky
author: Charlie Jane Anders

title: Colorless Tsukuru Tazaki and His Years of Pilgrimage
author: Haruki Murakami

title: Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone
author: J.K. Rowling

title: The Art of The Fellowship of the Ring
author: Gary Russell

title: The Old Man and the Sea
author: Ernest Hemingway
